description: Two independent delay lines, each free-running or locked to a clock, with feedback, a high-pass and a low-pass filter on the delayed signal, and crossfeed from the other line

params.text: Chooses whether that delay line runs free, its time taken straight from the TIME knob, or locks to the clock at CLK IN and delays by a note division.
Sets the delay: 1ms to 10 seconds when the line runs free, or one of twenty-five note divisions from a 1/128 triplet to 8 bars when it is synced. The display above shows the current setting.
Sets how much of that line's delayed signal is fed back into it, -100% to 100%; a negative setting feeds it back with its phase flipped.
Sets the cutoff of the low-pass filter on that line's delayed signal, 1kHz to 10kHz. Turning the knob down from the top of its travel switches the filter on, and a lamp shows that it is running.
Sets the cutoff of the high-pass filter on that line's delayed signal, 1kHz to 10kHz. Turning the knob up from the bottom of its travel switches the filter on, and a lamp shows that it is running.
Crossfades that line's main output between the signal coming in and the delayed signal.
Attenuates that line's input before it reaches both the delay and the dry path, 0% to 100%.
Feeds IN B into delay line A, from silence to full level, joining whatever IN A is carrying.
Feeds IN A into delay line B, from silence to full level, joining whatever IN B is carrying.
Empties that delay line's buffer, and lights red when it fires.

inputs.text: The clock the synced delay lines measure against; the gap between two rising edges is taken as a quarter note.
Adds a tenth of the TIME knob's travel per volt for that line, reading 0-10V.
Adds 10% of feedback per volt to that line's FEEDBACK knob.
Adds a tenth of the low-pass knob's travel per volt for that line, and patching a cable here switches the filter on whatever the knob is set to.
Adds a tenth of the high-pass knob's travel per volt for that line, and patching a cable here switches the filter on whatever the knob is set to.
Moves that line's DRY/WET mix 10% towards wet per volt.
The signal fed into that delay line.
A 10V trigger empties that delay line's buffer.

outputs.text: That line's incoming and delayed signals mixed by its DRY/WET knob.
That line's delayed signal alone, after its filters, with none of the incoming signal.

notes: a delay line switched to SYNC takes its tempo from CLK IN, the one jack both lines read; until two rising edges have arrived there it keeps the delay time it already had.
